items.question: By which four things is the quality of a cardiac screening examination judged?
options: Image quality, acquisition of the standard planes, interpretation of the views, and documentation
Scan duration, machine model, transducer type and gestational age
Number of images, colour Doppler use, 3D use and report length
Patient satisfaction, waiting time, cost and report turnaround
items.explanation: Quality assessment covers image quality, acquisition of the standard planes, appropriate interpretation and complete documentation.

items.question: Why should stills and clips of the cardiac views be archived?
options: So the examination can be reviewed later for adequacy
Only to give copies to the family
Because clips replace the written report
There is no recommendation to store them
items.explanation: Still frames and clips of the recommended views should be archived so the examination can later be reviewed for adequacy.

items.question: What should be labelled on stored images where appropriate?
options: Laterality and orientation
The examiner's opinion of the family history
The thermal index only
Nothing; labels reduce image quality
items.explanation: Stored images should carry labelling of laterality and orientation where appropriate.

items.question: For the outflow-tract and three-vessel planes, which is the more reliable record?
options: A cine clip
A single still frame of each
A written description alone
A measurement of each vessel
items.explanation: These planes are a continuum that varies with probe orientation and fetal lie; assessment is more reliable live or on cine-loop than from stills alone.

items.question: How often is a practice encouraged to review its detection rates and diagnostic accuracy?
options: Every year
Every ten years
Only when a diagnosis is missed
Never; this is the job of the referral centre
items.explanation: Annual review of local detection rates and accuracy is encouraged.

items.question: What is audit of stored images measured against?
options: Quality criteria set in advance
The examiner's memory of the scan
The length of the examination
The number of images stored
items.explanation: Audit against predetermined quality criteria for still images or clips is encouraged.

items.question: Your annual review shows that outflow-tract views were often not stored or not adequate. What does the guideline encourage?
options: Further training targeted at the gap
Dropping outflow-tract views from the protocol
No action unless a baby was harmed
Replacing the machine
items.explanation: Practices are encouraged to review their results and provide further training as needed; outflow-tract views are an integral part of the screen.

items.question: How large should the heart appear on the screen for a good-quality image?
options: At least a third to a half of the screen
About a tenth of the screen
Size on screen does not matter
The whole fetus should be in view with the heart
items.explanation: The image should be magnified until the heart fills at least one third to one half of the screen.

items.question: Which settings favour a good-quality cardiac image?
options: High frame rate, low persistence, a single focal zone and a narrow image field
Low frame rate, high persistence and a wide image field
Multiple focal zones and maximum depth
The general obstetric preset, unchanged
items.explanation: Settings should emphasise high frame rate, contrast and resolution, with low persistence, a single focal zone and a relatively narrow field; cardiac presets usually include these.

items.question: What did the 2023 screening guideline add?
options: Sections on quality assurance and on use of a checklist
A requirement for 3D imaging in every screen
Removal of the outflow-tract views
A requirement for pulsed-wave Doppler in every screen
items.explanation: The 2023 update encourages colour flow Doppler and adds sections on quality assurance and on use of a checklist.
